examples.title: Write your own rule over the whole graph
examples.summary: Plugins get the same resolved graph as the built-in rules. This one does the client-to-server check by hand.

blocks.label: team-rules.ts · Node 24, with sdk/ copied from the Archguard repository

examples.result: Plugin findings show up next to built-in findings, with the same exit codes. Rust rules use the same graph. archguard facts exports it as JSON.

examples.title: Find copy-pasted logic
examples.summary: Groups functions with the same structure, even after variables were renamed.
examples.result: You get pairs and groups of similar functions with their locations. Not every pair in a group matches. You decide what to merge.

examples.title: Find code changes your tests miss
examples.summary: Archguard makes small edits, like >= to >, and runs your tests on a copy to find changes they miss.

blocks.label: Run · mutator.json names the source files and your test command
Trimmed output · the bundled example's weak tests

examples.result: Each surviving edit names the line and the change. Some edits change nothing real, so read each one before adding a test. Archguard never edits your files. It works on copies.

examples.title: Let your agent try Archguard on your repo
examples.summary: Give your agent a time and disk budget. It looks for rules that fit, copy-pasted code, and test gaps.

blocks.label: Prompt for your agent
blocks.code:
Install the irudd-ts-evaluate skill from github.com/alundgren/irudd-ts
(skills/irudd-ts-evaluate) in your personal skills folder, not in this
repository. Use it to evaluate this repository.
You have eight hours and may use at most 20 GiB of disk, including setup.
Stop before free space falls below 12%.
You may create a draft PR here. Leave it open.

examples.result: The agent proposes rules backed by your docs or past fixes, and reports anything it could not check.
